'''Carlton Kaleel''' "'''Bub'''" '''Carrington III''' (born July 21, 2005) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]].

==Early life and high school career==
Carrington was born on July 21, 2005, in [[Baltimore|Baltimore, Maryland]], where he grew up.<ref name="auto4">{{Cite web|url=https://pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/carlton-carrington/12728|publisher=[[Pittsburgh Panthers]]|title=Carlton Carrington}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/4845374/carlton-carrington|publisher=[[ESPN]]|title=Carlton Carrington}}</ref> The third in his family with the same name, he was nicknamed "lil' bub" after the nickname of his father, a basketball coach, later shortened to just "bub".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2023/10/12/panthers-basketball-jaland-lowe-carlton-carrington-ncaa-college-hoops-acc/stories/202310110094|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|title=Guards Jaland Lowe and Carlton Carrington learn from physical practices and past Pitt leaders |author=Carter, Chrisopher|date=October 12, 2023}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2023/11/23/bub-carrington-jaland-lowe-thankful-thanksgiving-brooklyn-nit-season-tipoff/stories/202311230076|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|title=Pitt freshmen thankful to play in front of family during Thanksgiving trip to Brooklyn |date=November 23, 2023|author=Hiles, Noah}}</ref> He attended [[Saint Frances Academy (Baltimore)|Saint Frances Academy]] in Baltimore, where he played basketball, baseball and football.<ref name="auto4"/> He scored over 2,000 points in his high school career and after his [[Junior (education year)|junior]] year committed to playing college basketball for [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]], being ranked by [[247Sports]] a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], the 99th-best recruit overall, and the third-best player from the state.<ref name="auto4"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/pitt-basketball-recruiting-four-star-cg-carlton-carrington-commits-to-panthers-in-2023-class/|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]|title=Pitt basketball recruiting: Four-star CG Carlton Carrington commits to Panthers in 2023 class|date=June 15, 2022|author=Cobb, David}}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/recruiting/pitt-basketball-carlton-carrington-commits-panthers|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Four-Star G Carlton Carrington Commits To Pitt|date=June 15, 2023|author=Thompson, Stephen}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/pittsburgh-post-gazette/135718680/|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|author=McGonigal, Johnny|date=June 16, 2022|page=C9|title=Panthers sign Carrington for 2023}} {{Open access}}</ref> He chose Pittsburgh over eight other offers.<ref name="auto1"/>

Carrington also was a member of Team Melo in the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] travel circuit, being named the EYBL Breakout Player of the Session and second-team All-Session while helping the team reach a spot in the championships.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/recruiting/pitt-basketball-commit-carlton-carrington-named-eybl-breakout-player|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Pitt Basketball Commit Carlton Carrington Named EYBL Breakout Player of Session|author=Thompson, Stephen}}</ref> As a [[Senior (education)|senior]] at Saint Frances in 2022–23, Carrington helped the school have an overall record of 29–11 while going 11–3 in the [[Baltimore Catholic League]] (BCL); he was named first-team All-BCL and to the BCL All-Tournament team and averaged more than 26 points, seven rebounds, six assists and two steals per game.<ref name="auto4"/> He also led Saint Frances to the [[Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association]] (MIAA) tournament, which they won for the second time in his tenure, with Carrington being named to the All-Tournament team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pittsburghpanthers.com/news/2023/3/25/mens-basketball-carrington-named-to-capital-all-star-team.aspx|publisher=[[Pittsburgh Panthers]]|title=Carrington Named to Capital All-Star Team|date=March 25, 2023}}</ref> He had shooting splits of .490/.380/.860 and set a Saint Frances record with a total of more than 1,000 points scored.<ref name="auto4"/> He was invited to the DTLR Classic, Jumpman Classic, R1A Classic, More than Basketball Game and to the MLK Classic, earning [[most valuable player]] honors in each while setting a MLK Classic record with 42 points scored.<ref name="auto4"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/high-school-spotlight-2023-saint-james-mlk-classic-eye-catchers-part-one|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=High School Spotlight: 2023 Saint James MLK Classic Eye-Catchers (Part One)|date=January 17, 2023|author=Hines, Jam}}</ref> He was named a Capital All-Star, played at the 50th Annual Hoop Culture Capital Classic, and was All-Tournament at the City of Palms and Triple Threat Classics.<ref name="auto4"/>

==College career==
Carrington joined the Pittsburgh Panthers for the start of the [[2023–24 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|2023–24 season]] and became an immediate starter.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/basketball/bub-carrington-makes-pitt-panthers-history-college-debut|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Bub Carrington Makes Pitt History in College Debut|date=November 6, 2023|author=Thompson, Stephen}}</ref><ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/news/pitt-panthers-freshman-carlton-carrington-brings-superstar-potential|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Pitt Freshman Carlton Carrington Brings Superstar Potential|date=November 2, 2023}}</ref> He started in the exhibition opener against the [[University of Pittsburgh at Johnstown]] and the regular season opener against [[North Carolina A&T Aggies men's basketball|North Carolina A&T]].<ref name="auto3"/> Against North Carolina A&T, he helped the Panthers win 100–52 while totaling 18 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists for the first [[triple-double]] in a debut in school history and the second in [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) history, also being the first overall to accomplish the feat at Pittsburgh since 1998.<ref name="auto2"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/carlton-carrington-triple-double-paces-pitt-opener-2023-11-07/|agency=[[Reuters]]|title=Carlton Carrington triple-double paces Pitt in opener|date=November 6, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/2023/11/07/panthers-college-hoops-mens-basketball-acc-bub-carrington-jeff-capel/stories/202311060101|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|url-access=subscription|title=Freshman Bub Carrington is the first player in Pitt hoops history to record triple-double in debut |author=Carter, Christopher|date=November 7, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pittsburghpanthers.com/news/2023/11/13/mens-basketball-carrington-named-acc-rookie-of-the-week.aspx|publisher=[[Pittsburgh Panthers]]|title=Carrington Named ACC Rookie of the Week|date=November 13, 2023}}</ref> He was named the ACC Rookie of the Week and  received the honor again the following week, being the first Pittsburgh player to earn selection back-to-back since 2007–08.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.altoonamirror.com/sports/local-sports/2023/11/acc-keeps-noticing-pitt-freshman/|newspaper=[[Altoona Mirror]]|date=November 21, 2023|title=ACC keeps noticing Pitt freshman}}</ref>
